divided_by_variable_lost_root.name: Dividing both sides by the unknown
divided_by_variable_lost_root.why_students_do_it: Dividing by x looks like the same simplification as dividing by a constant, but it silently assumes x is not zero and therefore discards x = 0 as a solution.
divided_by_variable_lost_root.feedback_template: You divided both sides by x. That is only valid when x is not zero, so it quietly throws away the solution x = 0. Instead, move everything to one side and factorise.

dropped_plus_minus.name: Taking only the positive square root
dropped_plus_minus.why_students_do_it: The square-root symbol denotes the principal (positive) root, so students forget that solving x^2 = k requires both roots.
dropped_plus_minus.feedback_template: When you take the square root of both sides you must allow both signs. x^2 = k gives x = +sqrt(k) and x = -sqrt(k).
dropped_plus_minus.remediation_reference: Notes §3 — square roots and the plus-or-minus sign

sign_error.name: Sign error in factorising or rearranging
sign_error.why_students_do_it: When factorising x^2 + bx + c the signs of the two numbers depend on the signs of both b and c, and it is easy to reverse them.
sign_error.feedback_template: Check the signs in your factorisation. Expand your brackets and compare with the original equation — if they do not match, the signs are the usual culprit.

squaring_introduced_spurious_root.name: Squaring both sides introduced an extra solution
squaring_introduced_spurious_root.why_students_do_it: Squaring is not reversible, so it can create solutions that do not satisfy the original equation.
squaring_introduced_spurious_root.feedback_template: Squaring both sides can create solutions that do not work in the original equation. Always substitute your answers back to check.

lost_solution.name: A solution was lost during rearranging
lost_solution.why_students_do_it: Some manipulations quietly discard cases, particularly cancelling a common factor.
lost_solution.feedback_template: One of the solutions disappeared between two of your lines. Look for a step where you cancelled or divided by something that could be zero.

gained_solution.name: An extra solution appeared
gained_solution.why_students_do_it: A manipulation that is not reversible can introduce values that do not satisfy the original equation.
gained_solution.feedback_template: One of your answers does not satisfy the original equation. Substitute each answer back into the question to check.

no_working_shown.name: Answer given with no working
no_working_shown.why_students_do_it: The student may have solved it mentally or by calculator, but method marks cannot be awarded for working that is not shown.
no_working_shown.feedback_template: Your answer is correct, but there is no working to award method marks to. Show the rearrangement and the factorisation or formula you used.
no_working_shown.remediation_reference: Notes §0 — how your work is marked
